title: modal-stack-trapping-and-screenreader-order-cases
content:
Context:
This is a working notes doc capturing edge cases and proposed fixes for modal/dialog behavior in the Console. Goal is to unify behavior across: Create Job modal, Cluster Settings modal, Help/Keyboard Shortcuts modal, and nested confirmation dialogs (e.g., Delete inside modal). We’ve seen multiple customer reports where screenreader users lose context or keyboard focus escapes a modal stack during quick confirm flows.

Problem summary (high level):
- Modal stacking: When multiple dialogs are opened in sequence (modal -> confirm modal), focus trapping is inconsistent. Sometimes focus lands on the page behind the modal (esp. in Safari + NVDA through virtualization).
- Screenreader reading order: Use of portals (rendering modal at body root) + flex/grid visual ordering causes DOM order != visual order for some console panels, causing announcements like "dialog opened" but voice reads unrelated page sections first.
- Overlapping transient UI: Toasts and autosave banners occasionally interrupt focus/announce while modal is open, confusing users relying on screenreader focus.
- Nested focusable components: Datepickers/timepickers inside modals open their own popovers and sometimes lose the parent trap.
- Non-deterministic behavior across browsers and AT: Chrome+NVDA vs Safari+VoiceOver vs Firefox+NVDA show different failure modes.

Research summary (what we tested):
- Reproduced with NVDA+Chrome (Windows), VoiceOver+Safari (macOS), and NVDA+Firefox (Windows).
- Tested with Portal pattern (React), focus trap library (focus-trap-react), and a local inert-polyfill. Found that inert polyfill + overlay is the most consistent approach.
- Created small code playground reproducing stack-of-two-modals + toast. Confirmed the following failures: focus returned to body, first tabbable element behind overlay focused, screenreader reads DOM siblings that precede modal in DOM order.

Wireframe / interaction notes (quick sketches in words):
- Primary modal: full-sheet centered dialog with header (title + close), body (form controls), footer (primary + secondary actions).
- Confirmation modal (nested): smaller dialog centered over primary modal with high-contrast border. Action order: Cancel | Confirm (danger).
- Visual stacking indicator: subtle shadow + z-index token. Don’t rely on DOM order to communicate stacking — rely on aria-modal + inert overlay.

Proposed accessibility rules (core):
1) Always render modal contents as the last child of <body> (portal) to avoid incidental DOM siblings taking precedence.
2) Ensure aria-modal="true" on open dialogs and add role="dialog" + aria-labelledby pointing to visible header id.
3) Apply inert (or inert polyfill) to everything outside the top-most modal when any modal is open. For nested modals, only the top modal is focusable; lower modals remain inert.
4) Use focus-trap instituted at open: set focus to the first logical focusable element (primary CTA if appropriate, otherwise the dialog close). On close return focus to the element that triggered the open.
5) Pause non-essential live regions (toasts/notifications) while modal is open OR mark them aria-hidden="true" when inert applied to background.
6) For nested dialogs, set aria-hidden/aria-modal semantics so screenreader exposes only the top layer. Consider aria-flowto for complex flows (rare).
7) Avoid moving DOM nodes between portal root and original location while modal is open (keeps AT virtualization stable).

Edge case inventory (prioritized):
- EC1 (P0): Confirm-in-Modal -> user presses Enter, both modals accept due to mis-bound handlers. Root cause: event propagation + focus not clearly in top-level modal. Fix: stopPropagation on confirm handlers and ensure only active modal listeners run.
- EC2 (P0): Toast announces mid-modal open and steals virtual cursor. Fix: make toast role="status" updates suppressed when any modal open; or use aria-hidden on toast container when inert.
- EC3 (P1): Datepicker popup appears outside trap and becomes keyboard target (TAB jumps to datepicker fields then to page). Fix: attach popover to portal root and keep it controlled by parent trap.
- EC4 (P1): ESC closes only bottom modal in a stack (user expects topmost). Fix: ESC should close the topmost modal only. Validate by tracking modal id stack.
- EC5 (P2): Mobile voiceover reads off-screen elements when a sheet-style modal is used (not centered). Fix: use aria-modal and inert; for sheet variant test with NVDA/VoiceOver.

Detailed backlog items (candidate tickets):
- RWD-8321: Implement inert-overlay utility and apply globally to console root when modal open. (owner: eng-infra)
  - Acceptance: when a modal is open, document.querySelectorAll('#app-root > *:not(.modal-root)') are inert; keyboard cannot tab into them; screenreader does not announce them.
- RWD-8384: Modal focus manager overhaul: ensure focus returned to trigger, explicit focus order for nested dialogs. (owner: eng-ui)
  - Acceptance: single modal and two-layer nested modal tests pass in NVDA/Chrome and VoiceOver/Safari labs.
- RWD-8390: Pause toast live-region updates when modal open; add aria-live="polite" queueing. (owner: product-console)
  - Acceptance: open modal + trigger toast -> no immediate announcement until modal close OR toast marked hidden to AT.
- RWD-8412: Datepicker/popover portal alignment + trap integration. (owner: eng-ui)
  - Acceptance: datepicker opened inside modal remains reachable via arrow keys but does not allow TAB to escape top modal.
- RWD-8441: Keyboard shortcut sheet accessibility check (refs: slack thread). (owner: devexp)
  - Acceptance: sheet traps focus, escape closes, announcement reads title + first instruction.

Acceptance criteria (QA checklist):
- A1: Modal gets role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" and has aria-labelledby referencing header id.
- A2: On open focus moves to primary control; topmost modal traps tab/shift-tab; focus never moves to page content while modal open.
- A3: When nested, only topmost modal is interactive; lower modals present visually but inaccessible to AT and keyboard.
- A4: ESC closes topmost modal only; focus returns to last focused trigger.
- A5: Toasts should not interrupt or steal AT focus when modal open.
- A6: Datepicker/popover anchored elements do not allow TAB out of trap.
- A7: Performance: enabling inert overlay should not add >10ms to modal open on typical dev machine.

Testing matrix (initial automation + manual):
- Automated: Cypress + axe snapshots for role/aria attributes; unit tests for focus-trap manager.
- Manual: NVDA+Chrome (Windows), VoiceOver+Safari (macOS), TalkBack+Android (sheet variant), Firefox+NVDA. Test permutations: single modal, two stacked modals, modal + toast, modal with popover datepicker, modal open -> window blur/focus.

Developer implementation notes / code hints:
- Keep modal portal root at <div id="modal-root" aria-hidden="false"> and toggle inert on #app-root except .modal-root. Use window.requestAnimationFrame when toggling inert to avoid layout jitter.
- Use dataset modal-id and maintain a stack in ModalService (push/pop) rather than DOM querying for topmost.
- Example: on open -> ModalService.push(id) -> set body inert except modal-root -> set focus to firstElement. on close -> ModalService.pop(id) -> if stack empty remove inert.
- For ESC handling, bind to topmost modal only; keyboard listener checks ModalService.top() matches id.

Design / copy considerations:
- Modal announcement: header text should be clear and include context (e.g., "Create inference job — compute settings"). For confirm actions, include explicit consequence in the button label rather than adding long descriptions that force extra reading.
- For destructive confirms inside modals, add accessible name modification (e.g., "Confirm delete model: hoodie-v2") so SR users get specificity.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Feature-flag inert-overlay utility, run internal e2e and accessibility smoke tests. (week 1–2)
2) Replace modal instances incrementally: Job creation, Cluster Settings, Workflows modal (week 3–6).
3) Monitor error/feedback channels + run targeted external a11y audit with one customer.

Open questions / discussion points: 
- Should we completely suppress role="status" updates for all toasts or selectively queue only those that originated from modal interactions? (Tradeoff: critical system alerts might be missed.)
- Do we want to unify to a single ModalService or keep component-level traps for autonomy? (Service simplifies nested logic.)
- How to handle application-level keyboard shortcuts while any modal is open? Proposed: shortcut handlers check ModalService.isTopmostAllowShortcuts(), default false.

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: draft ModalService API and write two e2e scenarios for Cypress + NVDA smoke.
- Diego: prototype inert-overlay polyfill integration and measure perf.
- Sofia: prepare wireframes for stacked modals and update design tokens for z-index/shadow.
- Priya: compile final QA checklist for SRE and Product QA.

Notes to reviewers: this is an iterative working doc — please add comments inline or update linked Confluence spec. If you have direct AT test notes (VoiceOver/TalkBack) paste them into the slack thread referenced above.

Attachments / quick links (local):
- small-playground reproduction: github.com/redwood-inference/modal-playground (branch: a11y-modal-stack)
- comparative test results spreadsheet: /shared_drives/product/console-and-rollouts/a11y-modal-tests-2026-07.csv

End of doc.
